subject: QuantCap dedicated compute match and headroom request
messages:
From: Emma Thorpe <emma.thorpe@quantcap.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: QuantCap Procurement <procurement@quantcap.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — peak tokens/sec and latency targets

Hi Priyom / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. QuantCap is ready to scope a committed Dedicated plan but we need a firm match between our expected peak profile and the GPU slab you recommend. High level:

- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 sessions (interactive chat)
- Average response length: 400 tokens
- Peak token generation rate across the fleet: ~45,000 tokens/sec
- P95 latency target (generation only): <= 220 ms per token for 512-token responses (we recognize shorter prompts will be faster)

Can you provide a model / slab recommendation and a short calc showing tokens/sec per GPU, expected P95 token latency, and suggested operational headroom (safety multiplier)? We want to include this in our procurement packet for next-week exec signoff.

Attachments: sample request trace (we'll upload logs to the Drive link).

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Thorpe
Head of Product
QuantCap, Inc.
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Emma Thorpe <emma.thorpe@quantcap.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — peak tokens/sec and latency targets

Emma — thanks, this is exactly the kind of detail we need. Preliminary answers below; I'm attaching a quick compute spreadsheet with the math and two configuration options (conservative / optimized).

Short answers up front:
- Recommendation A (safe): run redwood-13b-ptq as the primary serving model. Expected sustained throughput per A100-80GB slab instance: ~9,000–10,500 tokens/sec depending on batching and request shape. To reach 45k peak tokens/sec with 1.5x headroom => ~6 slab GPUs. Expected P95 token latency (steady-state, 512 token generation) ~180–230 ms with our continuous-batching runtime and a 1.5x safety buffer.

- Recommendation B (cost-optimized): run redwood-7b-quant variant. Throughput per A100-80GB: ~16,000 tokens/sec with aggressive batching and prefix caching. To reach 45k peak with 1.5x headroom => ~3–4 GPUs. P95 token latency here is more sensitive to concurrency; expect ~220–300 ms at peak unless we add extra headroom or reserve burst capacity.

Assumptions and caveats:
- Numbers assume 80B-style latency benefits are not required; if you plan to use 70b-style models we need a different slab (far higher GPU count).
- We account for KV cache warming and an average token-compute mix consistent with chat-style generation (not heavy sampling or sampling temperature extremes).
- Headroom recommendation: 1.5x for normal committed plans, 2.0x if you require strict P95 under unpredictable spikes.

Next steps: if you can confirm whether latency or cost is the dominant constraint (and whether quantization level is acceptable), we can lock a formal proposal and a canary rollout plan.

Attachments: quantcap_compute_estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet with per-model calc).

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Thorpe <emma.thorpe@quantcap.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — operational notes and burst policy

Adding a few operational items we should include in the packet for procurement:

- Warm-up / cache priming: plan ~10 minutes of traffic or a synthetic priming pass to populate KV caches for common prompts — this materially reduces tail latency for the first requests after a cold start.
- Burst policy: recommend a committed slab sized to cover 1.5x nominal peak and keep a shared-burst pool for short spikes. We'll note the burst billing model and expected cost delta.
- Autoscaling and rollout: configure canary on 10% of traffic for the first 48 hours after cutover; watch P95 by route and roll back to a smaller model variant if regression >10%.
- Monitoring hooks: include a token-level latency trace (we'll provide a prebuilt Grafana dashboard).

For the numbers Priyom shared, ops-wise I'd bias toward Recommendation A if QuantCap wants predictable latency; Recommendation B is good if they prioritize lower committed cost and accept more aggressive scaling.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Thorpe <emma.thorpe@quantcap.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — dedicated slab recommendation (final)

Looping back after reviewing the spreadsheet and running a short internal micro-benchmark against redwood-13b-ptq with your approximate request distribution. Key items: 

- Measured sustained token/sec per A100-80GB (our infra, conservative batch config): 9.8k tokens/sec.
- P95 token latency (512-token gen) measured: 190 ms.
- Expected degradation window: under 2% of requests if the slab is sized at 6 GPUs and we implement the 1.5x headroom buffer.

Recommendation (final):
- Provision 6x A100-80GB reserved slab running redwood-13b-ptq as primary.
- Configure a 1.5x headroom target (45k peak -> reserve ~67.5k tokens/sec capacity), which maps to the 6 GPU slab above.
- Add a short-term shared-burst allowance (2x single-GPU equivalent) for flash spikes during launches.
- Rollout plan: canary 10% -> 50% over 72 hours with a rollback trigger if any route sees >12% P95 regression vs baseline.

I attached a short config doc with the exact runtime flags we recommend for the Dedicated slab and the compute estimate sheet for procurement.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-config.md, quantcap_compute_estimate.xlsx

If this looks good I can spin a formal quote (monthly committed slab) and an ops-SLA appendix for QuantCap.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
